pages.text: The Beam Diverter is a junction box for particle beams. It takes a beam in through one port and sends it back out through another, so a single $(l:multiblocks/accelerators/general)accelerator$(/l) can feed several $(l:multiblocks/particle_chambers/general)chambers$(/l) - or loop back into a $(l:multiblocks/accelerators/ring_accelerator)synchrotron$(/l) - without laying a separate beam line to each one.

pages.name: Beam Diverter
pages.text: A fixed $(l)5x5x5$() cube of Accelerator Casing and Glass. Corners must be casing. Other sizes will not form.

pages.title: Construction
pages.text: Inside, a cross of Accelerator Beam blocks links the four walls through the center. Above and below that center sits a single $(l:multiblocks/accelerators/general#dipole)dipole magnet$(/l) - an Accelerator Electromagnet top and bottom, with Accelerator Yokes filling the rest of the inner 3x3x3. The electromagnet's tier sets the diverter's bending strength.$(br2)Mount the Beam Diverter Controller anywhere in the casing.

pages.title: Beam Ports
pages.text: Each wall carries one Accelerator Beam Port at its center, for four ports in total. Set their modes with the $(l:multiblocks/multitool)multitool$(/l):$(br2)$(li)$(bold)Exactly one$() must be an $(l)input$().$(li)$(bold)At least one$() must be an $(l)output$().$(li)Spare ports can be left as output or disabled.$(br2)Ports can also be switched automatically with redstone or with a computer - see the Open Computers section.

pages.title: Diverting the Beam
pages.text: The incoming beam is pulled from the input port and pushed out the first active output. Sending it straight through (to the opposite wall) only costs the usual focus loss. Turning it 90 degrees to a side wall costs extra energy that scales with dipole strength, so a stronger electromagnet makes cheaper corners.$(br2)The controller draws power every tick it routes a beam; with an empty buffer it simply holds the beam and passes nothing.
